samples.summary: `ciConclusion` no longer verifies the runs belong to CI — the identity check now lives only in the two callers' URL strings, with nothing at runtime to enforce it
samples.evidence: The delta deletes `ciRunsFor` and changes `ciConclusion` to `newestRun(workflowRuns || [])` (checks.mjs:116-120), so the function trusts whatever list it is handed. Its own doc block still frames it as "CI's verdict for a SHA". Today both callers scope server-side (mark-ready.mjs:154, set-state.mjs:232), so nothing is currently broken — but the invariant that makes gate 1 unforgeable is now a naming convention plus a source-grep test (checks.test.mjs:536-548) hard-coded to exactly two filenames. A third caller, or a rewrite of either URL that keeps a `/runs?head_sha=` shape, hands unscoped runs to `ciConclusion` and gate 1 goes green on any workflow's newest run for the SHA, with no test failing. A cheap runtime guard (e.g. requiring every run's `workflow_id`/`path` to agree, or taking the workflow id as a parameter) would keep the check in the function that makes the decision.

samples.summary: The new workflow-scoped endpoint adds a 404 failure class that `catch { return false; }` reports as "CI is red", stalling promotion silently instead of exiting 2 as a tooling error
samples.evidence: `ciPassed` now calls `repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/workflows/${CI_WORKFLOW_FILE}/runs?head_sha=…` (mark-ready.mjs:152-155). Unlike the old `actions/runs?head_sha=` (which returns 200 with a list whenever the token can read Actions), this path 404s outright if `ci.yml` is ever renamed/removed or the workflow id cannot be resolved, and 403s without `actions: read`. Every one of those throws is swallowed by `catch { return false; }` at line 156-158, which is indistinguishable from a genuine red CI: the CLI prints "Not promoting: one or more gates are not satisfied" and exits 1, which agent-review-panel.yml:1539 treats as the benign "leaving as draft" outcome. A permanently unsatisfiable gate then looks exactly like an ordinary failing PR and never pages. mark-ready already reserves exit 2 for tooling errors (line 127); an API error reading gate 1 belongs there rather than in the gate-failed path.

finding.summary: The whole agent pipeline is now conditioned on `github.event.workflow_run.path`, a payload field nothing in the repo previously read and nothing validates — an empty/absent value disables panel, fixer and CI report with no page
finding.evidence: `grep` over `.github/` shows `github.event.workflow_run.path` appears only in the lines this diff adds (agent-review-panel.yml:117,166; agent-iterate-ci.yml:54; ci-report.yml:56); it is a first use. The tests exercise the clause only against synthetic PATH values injected into `new Function` (checks.test.mjs:183-218), never against a real payload. If the field is ever missing or differently populated (e.g. for the `requested` action, or a run created before a rename), the expression is false everywhere at once: the panel gate skips, the concurrency suffix resolves to 'noop', `stalled` is gated on `gate.outputs.managed` and therefore also skips, and no human is told. A single unverified field with a fail-silent blast radius over the whole loop.

verdict.reason: The path clause exists at the cited lines, but the asserted fail-silent mechanism does not. (a) The premise that `workflow_run.path` may be empty/absent is unsupported: the same gate expressions already depend, pre-existing, on sibling fields of the identical payload object — `head_repository.full_name`/`run_attempt` (agent-review-panel.yml:117,167,169), `conclusion` (agent-iterate-ci.yml:55), `event == 'pull_request'` (ci-report.yml:55), `head_branch`/`id` (ci-report.yml:39) — so an empty payload object would already have disabled the loop before this clause; `path` is a required property of the workflow_run object for both `requested` and `completed`. (b) The one concrete case named, a rename of ci.yml, is guarded at build time: checks.test.mjs:443-454 asserts CI_WORKFLOW_PATH names a file on disk whose runs are named `CI`, and checks.test.mjs:169-218 extracts the real `gate:` `if:` and concurrency `group:` from agent-review-panel.yml and asserts `partition("requested",1,CI_WORKFLOW_PATH) === "active"`, which fails the build if the yml literal drifts from the constant. (c) "No page" for a refused run is the deliberate `noop`-lane behavior documented at agent-review-panel.yml:95-110,216-218 and 2310-2321, identical to the pre-existing unmanaged/fork/disabled refusals, and checks.mjs:55-64 plus docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1904-1929,1966-1971 document the path comparison as the intended identity gate. The only residual — that agent-iterate-ci.yml:54 and ci-report.yml:56 literals are not pinned to the constant by a test — is test-coverage drift, not a reachable correctness fault.
